_comment: A1 Trading's published Top Setups board, transcribed from their own screen.
This is EVIDENCE, not configuration — nothing reads it at runtime. It exists so
`npm run parity` can score a change against their numbers instead of against an
impression formed by squinting at a browser table.
`totals` came from the score column, which is large and unambiguous.
`cells` is only filled for rows supplied at a resolution where every column was
legible, and each one was checked by summing it back to the published total
before being written down. Two so far; more make the per-slot attribution
sharper, and adding one is the single most useful contribution to this file.
Captured 2026-08-17, the same session as their US-DOLLAR Asset Scorecard. That
card reconciles against ours on all 18 cells, and XAGUSD, AUDUSD, NZDJPY,
NAS100, BTCUSD and ETHUSD match exactly, which is what pins the date.
